units.function: Credential-provider and real local Git-helper tests for resolving company/global GitHub tokens, scoping them to HTTPS GitHub hosts, redacting errors and attributing authentication failures.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> git-credentials service -> fake Secret service and real local git credential fill; no network, repository clone/fetch, database or real token is used.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Work/Run Secret access context, ordered Secret names, token source/name, Git remote URL, helper config/env invocation and scrubbed/auth-attributed failure.
units.lifecycle: Validate remote host/protocol -> resolve and memoize tenant Secret or global env fallback -> inject bearer through host-scoped Git helper env -> disable prompts -> scrub/classify failures.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 23/23, including three real local Git helper processes. Coverage strongly proves host/protocol helper scoping but omits credential rotation, managed-cloud fallback policy, child/hook exposure, clone/fetch races and provider-neutral enterprise Git.
units.designRationale: Authenticate server-managed Git without putting tokens in remote URLs or argv, make repository rewrites unable to redirect credentials to another host and offer actionable failure messages while avoiding false credential blame.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs customer-local, provider-neutral source-data credentials with explicit tenant/repository/purpose scope, short lifetime, auditable use and immediate revocation across managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the empty-default helper, exact host/protocol scoping, no-argv token rule, prompt disabling, real helper regression and safe failure attribution inside a Git DataConnector. Replace ordered ambient names/global fallback with SecretPort-issued repository/audience/TTL-bound grants, deployment-profile policy, explicit tenant consent and rotation-aware non-plaintext caching.
units.responsibilityConflict: A fixed system consumer may resolve a company token with Work/Run context but no accountable human, ResponsibilityContract, DataAuthorization or approval. Global server fallback can silently change which legal party's credential performs a tenant action.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL managed-cloud risk: tenant Secret failure/absence can fall back to a platform-global bearer credential without demonstrated tenant consent. HIGH revocation gap: plaintext resolution is memoized with no TTL/invalidation. HIGH bearer exposure: token remains in child environment and can reach Git hooks/descendants/core dumps. HIGH scope gap: credential is host-wide rather than repository/action/audience-bound. HIGH provider gap: enterprise/GitLab/Gitee/local Connector cases are unsupported. MEDIUM redaction gap: arbitrary prose/path/header tokens are not covered.
